root_cause: The 'GatedDeltaNet Fusion Test' step installs its own requirements file (gated_delta_net.txt, pinning optimum-intel==2.2.0 and transformers==4.57.6) into a venv shared across all PyTorch Models tests sub-steps that run sequentially in the same job/container. An earlier sub-step in the same job (optimum_intel.txt install) pulled in a 'datasets'/'pyarrow' stack that requires NumPy>=2.0, while the venv's installed NumPy stayed pinned at 1.26.4 (a dependency of an earlier-installed, older torch/transformers combination). pip's resolver, warned about in the preceding 'dependency conflicts' messages, does not uninstall/upgrade numpy when installing the later gated_delta_net requirements, so by the time the GatedDeltaNet test module imports `datasets` -> `pyarrow`, pyarrow's compiled extension (built against NumPy ABI 2.x) refuses to initialize against the older NumPy 1.26.4 still present in site-packages. This is a transitive dependency/version-skew problem across sequential per-test pip installs in one shared venv, not a bug in the GatedDeltaNet transformation or test code itself.
reproduction_steps: In a fresh venv (python3.11): 1) pip install -r install/tests/model_hub_tests/pytorch/envs/optimum_intel.txt (installs numpy 1.26.4 transitively via older torch/transformers chain); 2) pip install -r install/tests/model_hub_tests/pytorch/envs/gated_delta_net.txt (installs optimum-intel==2.2.0, transformers==4.57.6, pulling a newer 'datasets'/'pyarrow' stack) without upgrading numpy; 3) python3 -c "from optimum.intel import OVModelForCausalLM" -> reproduces the ImportError: pyarrow requires NumPy 2.0 or newer, found 1.26.4.
recommended_actions: Pin or upgrade numpy explicitly in tests/model_hub_tests/pytorch/envs/gated_delta_net.txt (and/or optimum_intel.txt) to a version >=2.0 compatible with the pinned pyarrow/datasets stack, or pin pyarrow/datasets to versions compatible with numpy 1.26.x.

Run each PyTorch model-hub test group (optimum_intel, gated_delta_net, moe, etc.) in an isolated venv/container instead of sequentially reusing one shared venv, to avoid cross-test transitive dependency skew.

Add a CI sanity check (e.g., 'pip check' or an explicit import smoke test) immediately after each requirements install step to fail fast with a clearer dependency-conflict message instead of only pytest collection errors.
Review tests/model_hub_tests/pytorch/envs/*.txt files for numpy pinning consistency across all per-model requirement files used by the same job.
prevention_strategies: Isolate per-test-suite Python dependency installs (venv-per-suite or constraints file shared across all requirement files in the job) so that a later install step cannot silently leave an earlier, incompatible package version (numpy) installed while pulling in a package (pyarrow) that hard-requires a newer ABI-incompatible version. Add automated 'pip check' / import-smoke-test gating after dependency installation steps in CI.
historical_context: No prior post-commit investigation in this knowledge base matches this exact pyarrow/NumPy ABI mismatch signature; it is a new, distinct pattern. Other known recurring infra patterns (ARM64 cross-compilation cc1plus invalid-pch, pip-proxy malformed JSON) are unrelated dependency/toolchain issues.
